html:
The Tariana are an Arawakan-speaking people of the middle Vaupés River in the northwest Amazon, on the border between Brazil and Colombia. They came into the Vaupés from Arawakan lands to the north and live among Tukanoan peoples, such as the Tukano and Karapana.

The Vaupés peoples marry across language lines, and over generations the Tariana have been shifting to the Tukano language; only a small number still speak Tariana, which linguists study as a famous case of languages blending. They live in riverside villages, growing manioc and fishing. Salesian missions dominated the region in the 1900s. Their Arawakan relatives include the Baniwa. See Brazil.
